advice: Experiment: change only the two main tile traversals around `Llibxsmm_440` and the outer `Llibxsmm_64` loop. Current order is outer 64-row bands, then 32-column panels; each panel computes two adjacent 32-row tiles using the packed A scratch. Test swapping those traversal levels: hold one 32-column panel fixed while visiting successive 64-row bands, preserving the two 32-row tiles per band and the existing K loops, packing, and stores. Keep the full K reduction and write each output tile once. Hypothesis: changing panel reuse and C write locality may improve throughput; this is unverified advice, not a measured fact.
risks: Reordering changes when A is packed and how long packed data remains useful; the existing scratch contents and pointer resets may not support the swapped loops without careful address and lifetime changes. It may increase repacking or loop overhead. Check every tile is visited exactly once, preserve all pointer bounds and ABI state, retain the complete BSD notice, and validate n=512 plus general odd/tail sizes and n<=0 at tolerance 0.002. Then use fresh repeated paired controls with power source and settings unchanged. Do not infer causality from noisy scores or credit a joint outcome to this proposal alone.
